newsitem.title: USA: Cell Robotics gets OK for Lasette study. [CORRECTED 18:45 GMT]
newsitem.headline: Cell Robotics gets OK for Lasette study. [CORRECTED 18:45 GMT]

text.p: Cell Robotics International Inc said on Monday it has received final approval from the Food and Drug Administration for a clinical study of its Lasette, a laser finger perforator.
Lasette is used for sampling capillary blood for glucose and other blood chemistry readings.
Clinial trials were initiated under an FDA conditional investigational device exemption that was granted in August. Those trials are currently under way.
It received final approval after the company made some agreed-upon changes to the testing protocol.
The company plans to submit a 510K application in November 1996 (corrects from 1997) to seek approval for full marketing status of Lasette.
Cell Robotics said that between 20 and 50 preproduction prototypes will be constructed by the end of the year.
